content: Standard false-positive suppression stack in alerting: (a) require N consecutive failing checks before firing (debounce / pending period); (b) hysteresis - different thresholds for entering vs exiting alert state, so recovery needs a stronger signal than failure; (c) cooldown / debounce window suppressing repeated notifications - pitfall is a too-long window hiding persistent issues; (d) flap detection collapsing a storm of state transitions into one 'this is unstable' notice; (e) deduplication/grouping so multiple sources of the same condition produce one notification; (f) keep_firing_for / recovery threshold to avoid rapid resolve-then-fire churn. Grafana names these Pending period, Keep firing for (Recovering state), and No Data/Error state handling with 'missing series evaluations to resolve' for staleness. Explicit tradeoff: hysteresis delays detection of real problems.
